data.turoyo: W mhərre, maqəmme suhḏe baynoṯayye: ayna d qoləb, hawo gmiǧaze.
data.translation: Sie drückten das Siegel darauf und stellten Zeugen zwischen sich auf: wer umfällt, wird bestraft.

rationale: Thin Preterit sense 1 cell: plural sealing parties and witnessed agreement context, contrasting with the existing singular letter-sealing example.

summary: PrS 9/9 exactly duplicates the existing letter-and-seal quotation under prs 20/21, and 111/7 is already the Imperativ example. Only 61/319 adds a previously unrepresented contextual attestation.

mhərre has a plural agent with the l-series ending assimilated after r. The sealed item is unexpressed in the supplied verse; witnesses and the penalty clause support formal agreement, but the reader's sanade from /318 cannot be independently checked here.

The inherited sense 1 combines physical sealing and electing a candidate. These occurrences corroborate that editorial grouping, without forcing a new numbered sense or a new political technical sense.

Letter sealing uses a b-instrument bu məhər diḏe; election uses the candidate l-suffix in mharuli, matching the existing Infectum l-muxtār example. No Detransitive or new collocation is established by the cognate seal noun.
Please reconcile inherited prs 20/21 with supplied PrS 9/9 before changing the citation.
Can the preceding /318 document be checked to identify the implicit object of mhərre at 61/319? This run does not quote or invent that unavailable clause.
